messages:
sam: FYI last night we got ~40 pages from gpu-pool-eu-west between 02:10-02:30 UTC. Most were 1-2m flares, different nodes each time. low impact but noisy.
lina: ugh saw that. majority were OOM-ish logs but then recovered. paging for 1-min blips is hurting oncall.
jordan: can you paste a sample alert? think we already have debounce and grouping but maybe cardinality spikes bypass it.
sam: here's one alert snippet from Prometheus:
```
ALERT GPU_Flare_High
IF increase(gpu_error_total{pool="gpu-pool-eu-west"}[1m]) > 5
FOR 0m
LABELS {severity="page", team="infra"}
ANNOTATIONS {summary="gpu pool flare"}
```
maria: FOR 0m is the issue. short flares -> immediate page. We should avoid FOR 0m for high-cardinality signals.
lina: agree. suggestion: change policy to ticket when cardinality > N and keep paging for low-cardinality (node-level) events that indicate a systemic problem.
sam: exactly. propose heuristic:
- compute cardinality = count_over_time(gpu_error_total{pool="gpu-pool-eu-west"}[5m]) by (node)
- if distinct_nodes > 3 -> create ticket (severity=low), else page
or more generically:
  severity = page if distinct_nodes <= 3 and spike_rate > threshold
  else ticket
jordan: math variant i like: adaptive threshold = base_threshold * sqrt(distinct_nodes). avoids hard cutoffs.
maria: we can implement in Alertmanager routes: route by matcher "distinct_nodes > 3" -> ticket receiver; else page receiver.
opsbot: deploy-bot: created branch "ops/alert-burst-suppression" with proposed rule changes.
lina: also add smoothing in PromQL to ignore micro-bursts: e.g.
```
(sum(increase(gpu_error_total{pool="gpu-pool-eu-west"}[1m]))
  / max(1, count_distinct(node_label)))
  > 0.8
```
(not exact but shows idea)
sam: another idea: add a short refractory mute per node after a page (e.g., 10m) to prevent retries from the same node bumping us again, but still count node toward cardinality.
jordan: careful: mute vs silence; we want to avoid missing real repeated failures. Use decline if same node repeats -> ticket if it persists after X repeats.
maria: also tie mute windows to scheduled infra jobs. if we know we ran nightly GC at 02:00 in eu-west, mute for that window (with annotation) to avoid noise.
lina: ops note: grouping by failure_reason label helps collapse similar alerts: group_key: {{pool}}:{{failure_reason}}.
sam: runbook change: add section "burst suppression" that describes the three axes: cardinality, duration, and severity mapping.
jordan: metrics/dashboard: add a small Grafana panel that shows "alert cardinality over time" and a heatmap of nodes firing. helps debug whether flares are systemic.
maria: quick PromQL for cardinality heatmap suggestion:
```
count by (node) (increase(gpu_error_total{pool="gpu-pool-eu-west"}[5m]))
```
then use transform in panel.
lina: action items:
- sam -> open PR adjusting FOR and adding cardinality-based route (today)
- jordan -> grafana card panel + dashboard row (tomorrow)
- maria -> update runbook and add scheduled mute annotations (today)
- opsbot -> after PR, deploy-bot will run smoke tests and post results
sam: +1. I'll draft PR with adaptive threshold example and refractory snippet.
maria: also add a note to SLO dashboard that pages caused by transient flares should be filtered out of page-count SLOs (separate metric for sustained incidents).
jordan: can we also add a cheap gating rule to Alertmanager that suppresses paging if a recent deploy happened in the window? many flares coincide with deploy noise.
lina: yes use webhook from deploy-bot with annotation "recent_deploy=true" and route to ticket.
deploy-bot: annotation added: "last_deploy_ts=2142338000" for recent deploys.
sam: thanks. if nobody objects i'll open the PR in ~1h and include the example PromQL + Alertmanager route.
lina: no objections. :thumbsup:
maria: sounds good. saves oncall cycles.
opsbot: reminder: testing in staging first. will forward test results here.
